stories.headline: Labour leadership crisis deepens as Blair critique, Burnham succession plans and Mandelson file release dominate the week
stories.summary: A 5,700-word essay by former PM Tony Blair accusing the Starmer government of having 'no coherent plan' triggered a week of intense political coverage, with Starmer publishing a Substack rebuttal, leadership challengers Wes Streeting and Andy Burnham distancing themselves from key government policies, and parliament compelling the government to release private messages involving disgraced former ambassador Peter Mandelson. Reports emerged that Starmer's allies have drawn up a six-month handover plan to Burnham, who signalled openness to an early general election if he wins the Makerfield by-election and succeeds Starmer.

stories.headline: GCHQ director's inaugural Bletchley Park lecture warns of Russian hybrid warfare, AI threats, and announces national cyber shield
stories.summary: GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler delivered the agency's first-ever annual public lecture at Bletchley Park on Wednesday 27 May, warning that the UK is at a 'moment of consequence' as Russia 'relentlessly targets' UK infrastructure and democratic processes, and that the window to maintain technological advantage over adversaries is narrowing. She announced plans for a world-first national AI cyber defence shield, revealed that GCHQ estimates nearly 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, and issued a notably softer tone on China compared to Russia.

stories.headline: AUKUS ministers at Shangri-La Dialogue announce undersea drone programme and revise submarine deal as Healey calls for delivery over talk
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey met US and Australian counterparts at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore on 30 May, announcing the first-ever AUKUS Pillar II 'signature project' — a jointly developed suite of unmanned undersea vehicles (UUVs) to be delivered by 2027 — and confirming that Australia will now receive only second-hand Virginia-class submarines rather than a mix of new and used boats. Healey acknowledged that AUKUS had 'talked too much and delivered too little' and committed UK spending of over £150 million to the drone project; the ministers also set 2027 as the deadline to stand up submarine rotational operations in Western Australia.
